prompts:
A database newsletter's fact-check desk needs three facts confirmed before Friday's issue goes out, each against a primary source: the project's or the standards body's own website, not a wiki or a news story. This one needs the open web, and you are allowed to browse.

- `sqlite_3_40_0_release_date`: the release date of SQLite 3.40.0
- `postgresql_15_0_release_date`: the release date of PostgreSQL 15.0
- `unicode_15_0_characters_added`: how many characters Unicode 15.0 added

Record them in {WS}/result.json, one entry per key above, each an object with `value` (a date as YYYY-MM-DD, a count as a number) and `url` (the primary-source page that shows it).
answers: [goal] Confirm three facts against primary sources, record in `./result.json`. [action] Wrote `result.json`, then fetched each primary page with curl and matched the values. No browser tabs or apps were opened, so nothing to close. [result] All three confirmed by the fetched pages; quoted lines are the exact grep output: | Key | Value | Primary source | Matched text | |---|---|---|---| | `sqlite_3_40_0_release_date` | 2022-11-16 | https://www.sqlite.org/releaselog/3_40_0.html | `3.40.0 On 2022-11-16` | | `postgresql_15_0_release_date` | 2022-10-13 | https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/15.0/ | `Release date: 2022-10-13` | | `unicode_15_0_characters_added` | 4489 | https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode15.0.0/ | `0 adds 4,489 characters,` and `4,489 characters have been added` | Assumptions: - "PostgreSQL 15.0" means the first general-availability release of version 15, as dated in its own release notes. - The Unicode count is the Consortium's own stated figure on the version page. - Dates are as printed by each project, with no timezone adjustment. [next] None; ready for Friday's issue.
